claim: Three rhesus monkeys (Macaca mulatta), aged 4–6 years, were used in the study.
source: Three rhesus monkeys (Macaca mulatta), aged 4–6 years, underwent two sequential surgeries under general anesthesia and strict sterile conditions.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: A 20 mm diameter craniotomy was performed on the skull over V1 during the initial surgery.
source: During the initial surgery, a 20 mm diameter craniotomy was performed on the skull over V1.
evidence: This describes the surgical procedure used in the study.

claim: AAV1.hSynap.GCaMP5G.WPRE.SV40 was pressure-injected at a depth of approximately 350 μm.
source: The dura was opened, and multiple tracks of 100–150 nL AAV1.hSynap.GCaMP5G.WPRE.SV40 (AV-1-PV2478, titer 2.37e13 (GC/ml), Penn Vector Core) were pressure-injected at a depth of approximately 350 μm.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: The procedures were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee, Peking University.
source: The procedures were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee, Peking University.
evidence: This describes the ethical approval for the study.

claim: Eye positions were monitored by an ISCAN ETL-200 infrared eye-tracking system at a sampling rate of 120 Hz for Monkeys A and B.
source: They were trained to maintain fixation on a small white spot (0.1°), with eye positions monitored by an ISCAN ETL-200 infrared eye-tracking system (ISCAN Inc) at a sampling rate of 120 Hz for Monkeys A and B, and an Eyelink-1000 (SR Research) at a sampling rate of 1000 Hz for Monkey C.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Eye positions were monitored by an Eyelink-1000 at a sampling rate of 1000 Hz for Monkey C.
source: They were trained to maintain fixation on a small white spot (0.1°), with eye positions monitored by an ISCAN ETL-200 infrared eye-tracking system (ISCAN Inc) at a sampling rate of 120 Hz for Monkeys A and B, and an Eyelink-1000 (SR Research) at a sampling rate of 1000 Hz for Monkey C.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Trials in which the eye position deviated 1.5° or more from the fixation point before stimulus offset were excluded as ones with saccades and repeated.
source: During the experiment, trials in which the eye position deviated 1.5o or more from the fixation point before stimulus offset were excluded as ones with saccades and repeated.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Eye positions were within 0.5° from the fixation point in over 95% of trials.
source: For the remaining trials, the eye positions were predominantly concentrated around the fixation point, with eye positions within 0.5o from the fixation point in over 95% of trials.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: Visual stimuli were generated using a ViSaGe system for Monkeys A and B.
source: For Monkeys A and B, visual stimuli were generated using a ViSaGe system (Cambridge Research Systems) and presented on a 21'' Sony G520 CRT monitor with a refresh rate of 80 Hz, a resolution of 1280 pixel ×960 pixel, and a pixel size of 0.31 mm × 0.31 mm.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Visual stimuli were created using Psychotoolbox 3 for Monkey C.
source: For Monkey C, visual stimuli were created using Psychotoolbox 3 (Pelli and Zhang, 1991) and presented on a 27'' Acer XB271HU LCD monitor with a refresh rate of 80 Hz native, a resolution of 2560 pixel ×1,440 pixel native, and a pixel size of 0.23 mm × 0.23 mm.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Each stimulus was presented for 1000 ms, followed by an inter-stimulus interval of 1500 ms.
source: Each stimulus was presented for 1000 ms, followed by an inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 1500 ms, allowing sufficient time for the calcium signals to return to baseline levels (Guan et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Each stimulus condition was repeated 12 times, with six repetitions for each opposite drift direction.
source: Each stimulus condition was repeated 12 times, with six repetitions for each opposite drift direction.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: When presenting a stimulus monocularly to one eye, the other eye was covered with a translucent eye patch to minimize short-term monocular deprivation.
source: When presenting a stimulus monocularly to one eye, the other eye was covered with a translucent eye patch to minimize short-term monocular deprivation.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Two-photon calcium imaging was performed with a Prairie Ultima IV two-photon microscope on Monkeys A and B.
source: Two-photon calcium imaging was performed with a Prairie Ultima IV (In Vivo) two-photon microscope (Prairie Technologies) on Monkeys A and B, or a FENTOSmart two-photon microscope (Femtonics) on Monkey C, and a Ti:sapphire laser (Mai Tai eHP, Spectra Physics).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Two-photon calcium imaging was performed with a FENTOSmart two-photon microscope on Monkey C.
source: Two-photon calcium imaging was performed with a Prairie Ultima IV (In Vivo) two-photon microscope (Prairie Technologies) on Monkeys A and B, or a FENTOSmart two-photon microscope (Femtonics) on Monkey C, and a Ti:sapphire laser (Mai Tai eHP, Spectra Physics).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: GCaMP5 was chosen as the indicator of calcium signals because the fluorescence activities it expresses are linearly proportional to neuronal spike activities within a wide range of firing rates from 10 to 150 Hz.
source: GCaMP5 was chosen as the indicator of calcium signals because the fluorescence activities it expresses are linearly proportional to neuronal spike activities within a wide range of firing rates from 10 to 150 Hz (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior methodological study.

claim: One FOV of 850 x 850 μm² was selected from each animal and imaged using a 1000 nm femtosecond laser under a 16× objective lens at a resolution of 1.6 μm/pixel.
source: One FOV of 850 x 850 μm2 was selected from each animal and imaged using a 1000 nm femtosecond laser under a 16× objective lens (0.8 N.A., Nikon) at a resolution of 1.6 μm/pixel.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: A fast resonant scanning mode (32 frames per second) was chosen to obtain continuous images of neuronal activity (8 frames per second after averaging every 4 frames).
source: A fast resonant scanning mode (32 frames per second) was chosen to obtain continuous images of neuronal activity (8 frames per second after averaging every 4 frames).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: A normalized cross-correlation based translation algorithm was used to reduce motion artifacts.
source: A normalized cross-correlation based translation algorithm (source code provided in Source code 1) was used to reduce motion artifacts (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology used in the study.

claim: A non-parametric Friedman test was performed to test whether a neuron's responses at 12 orientations or 6 SFs were significantly different from each other at least under one monocular stimulation condition.
source: Second, to select orientation and/or SF tuned neurons, a non-parametric Friedman test was performed to test whether a neuron's responses at 12 orientations or 6 SFs were significantly different from each other at least under one monocular stimulation condition.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology used in the study.

claim: The significance level was set at α=0.01 to reduce Type-I errors.
source: To reduce Type-I errors, the significance level was set at α=0.01.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology used in the study.

claim: Only neurons with goodness of fit R² >0.5 at least under one stimulation condition were finally selected as orientation-tuned neurons.
source: Only neurons with goodness of fit R2 >0.5 at least under one stimulation condition were finally selected as orientation-tuned neurons.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology used in the study.

claim: Only neurons with goodness of fit R² >0.5 at least under one monocular stimulation condition were selected as SF tuned neurons.
source: Only those with goodness of fit R2 >0.5 at least under one monocular stimulation condition were selected as SF tuned neurons.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology used in the study.
